documents.title: Arithmetic to algebra
documents.summary: A bounded path that makes arithmetic laws explicit, applies them to factored equations, and returns to signed-number operations.
objectives: Distinguish Course order from learner prerequisites.
Move among narrative, examples, exercises, and exact formal provenance.

documents.title: Natural-number operations
documents.summary: Natural-number operation laws form the arithmetic-to-algebra spine of the slice.
objectives: Recognize identity, associativity, commutativity, distributivity, and cancellation as named structures.
Use the laws in concrete natural-number examples.

documents.title: Distribute and cancel
documents.summary: A unit connecting the distributive law with cancellation of a common addend.
objectives: Distribute multiplication to both addends.
Cancel an equal common addend before evaluating an expression.

documents.title: Natural-number operation laws
documents.summary: A bounded view of natural-number identities, associativity, commutativity, distributivity, and additive cancellation.
objectives: Read familiar computations as instances of reusable law schemas.
Separate the instructional scope from the more general library structure used to verify it.

documents.title: Natural-number law examples
documents.summary: Two kernel-checked examples show distribution and cancellation without pretending to replace the canonical laws.
objectives: Cancel the common left addend 9 from an equality.

documents.title: Distribute-and-cancel exercise
documents.summary: A guided distributive-law exercise checks cancellation, full distribution, and the final natural-number value as three separate steps.
objectives: Cancel a common addend from both sides.
Distribute to both addends.
Verify the final value and reject a one-addend distribution error.

documents.title: Signed-number operations
documents.summary: A bounded return to arithmetic operations with integer signs.
objectives: Interpret subtraction of a negative as addition.
Interpret a product of two negative integers as positive.

documents.title: Integer sign laws
documents.summary: A unit for subtraction of a negative and multiplication of two negatives.
objectives: Connect sign rules to additive-group and ring structure.
Keep concrete examples distinct from general laws.

documents.title: Integer operation and sign laws
documents.summary: A bounded view of additive inverses, subtraction of a negative, and multiplication of two negatives.
objectives: Rewrite subtraction of a negative as addition.
Explain the positive product of two negative integers within the bounded integer treatment.

documents.title: Integer sign-law examples
documents.summary: Two concrete examples compute seven minus negative three and negative seven times negative four.
objectives: Evaluate 7-(-3).
Evaluate (-7)(-4).

documents.title: Factored expressions and equations
documents.summary: A bounded branch from a factored integer expression to its zero-product solution characterization.
objectives: Read a factored expression as a named construction.
Connect zero product with the two displayed roots.

documents.title: Zero-product method
documents.summary: A unit for recognizing the roots displayed by a factored integer equation.
objectives: Interpret (x-a)(x-b)=0.
Check the roots a and b without expanding the product.

documents.title: Factored integer expression
documents.summary: The expression (x-a)(x-b) is the bounded factored-product construction used by this slice.
objectives: Identify the two displayed linear factors.
Evaluate the expression at a proposed integer root.

documents.title: Zero-product characterization
documents.summary: The selected factored integer product is zero exactly when x equals one of its displayed roots.
objectives: Read the equivalence between a zero product and its two roots.
Keep proof dependencies distinct from learner prerequisites.

documents.title: Roots two and five
documents.summary: The equation (x-2)(x-5)=0 has exactly the integer roots 2 and 5.
objectives: Specialize the general zero-product characterization.
Read explicit unavailable and needs-review external-classification states.
